correctness.rationale: In each row least squares gives e_i=h·g_i/||g_i||² almost surely and Y_i=e_i² equals the excess squared row error by orthogonality. The Gaussian vector h is independent of the pair of regressors; their block covariance has identity diagonal and ρI off-diagonal. Standardizing the conditional numerator gives a unit normal independent of ||g_i||², so the F_{1,q}/q law and inverse-chi-square mean 1/(q−2) follow. Independently of the spherical integral in the paper, the scaled exceedance region |h·u|>||u||² is the disjoint union of open balls centered at ±h/2 with radius ||h||/2, of volume J=2^(1−q)π^(q/2)||h||^q/Γ(q/2+1). For |ρ|<1 put u_i=√t g_i: the Jacobian gives t^(−q), and the joint Gaussian density at the origin is (2π)^(−q)(1−ρ²)^(−q/2). Its exponential factor is at most one and tends to one on the product of the two regions; E J² is finite, so dominated convergence applies. Using E||h||^s=2^(s/2)Γ((q+s)/2)/Γ(q/2), the marginal limit constant is (2π)^(−q/2)E J=C_q and the joint numerator is (2π)^(−q)E J²=K_q by gamma duplication. The orthogonal product ratio is E J²/(E J)²>1 by strict variance, equal to the stated gamma ratio. For ρ=±1 the regressors are equal up to sign and the squared errors coincide, giving the separate t^(−q/2) law. At q=3 these checks give C_3=4/(3π) and K_3=35/(24π). All limits are fixed-angle and the nonaligned coefficient diverges toward either alignment boundary, consistent with nonuniformity.
residual_risks: The supplied importance-sampling estimates are finite-threshold diagnostics for q=3 and a few correlations; they neither certify the tail limits nor justify extrapolation toward alignment. The analytic density and moment argument supplies the claimed limits.
The mean formula uses q>2; the assertions do not cover varying sketch size or correlation with t.

evidence: The marginal law and exact signed-alignment identity determine the aligned branch once the common residual is specified; the same marginal law also holds with nonaligned directions and does not determine the product-normalized limit there. Conditional on h for ρ=0 the two events are independent, with leading rates proportional to the same ||h||^q.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: An independent pair with these same marginal laws would have joint coefficient C_q² at ρ=0; the given joint coefficient involves a strictly larger second moment. The single-row or ordinary multivariate model does not imply this, and no stronger theorem covering the actual paired law was established by the inspected texts.

evidence: The algorithm corresponds exactly to rank-one per-row regression against Gᵀv_i. The earlier beta-prime formula with residual rank one and degrees of freedom q gives F_{1,q}/q exactly. The sketch-regression paper gives a normal/chi-square representation and multivariate Student law for a complete-sketch estimator.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Student marginals do not give an ordinary multivariate Student vector here: at ρ=0 the regressor norms are independent, the conditional extreme rates share a fluctuating residual, and the joint exponent is twice the marginal one. This paired regression is not Gaussian scores over a common chi-square denominator.

value.rationale: A shared Gaussian sketch is a natural algorithmic choice, and neither the exact mean nor the marginal law reveals simultaneous catastrophic errors. The exponent changes at alignment without changing either marginal, and orthogonality still leaves a nontrivial factor above independent risk. The coefficient and its divergence as alignment is approached quantify how far independent-error heuristics can fail, and offer a sharp reference for future multirow or uniform-alignment analysis without asserting either extension.
residual_risks: The quantitative value is a fixed-angle tail comparison for shared identical residuals; practical guarantees at a finite threshold near alignment require separate analysis.
